272: However different from traditional attention method, the constraint of ∑iwi=1\sum_{i}w_{i}=1 is relaxed in Eq.(3), aiming to reserve the intensity of user interests.
273: That is, normalization with softmax on the output of a⁡(⋅)a(\cdot) is abandoned.
274: Instead, value of ∑iwi\sum_{i}w_{i} is treated as an approximation of the intensity of activated user interests to some degree.
275: For example, if one user’s historical behaviors contain 90% clothes and 10% electronics.
276: Given two candidate ads of T-shirt and phone, T-shirt activates most of the historical behaviors belonging to clothes and may get larger value of 𝒗U\bm{v}_{U} (higher intensity of interest) than phone.
277: Traditional attention methods lose the resolution on the numerical scale of 𝒗U\bm{v}_{U} by normalizing of the output of a⁡(⋅)a(\cdot).
278: We have tried LSTM to model user historical behavior data in the sequential manner.
279: But it shows no improvement.
280: Different from text which is under the constraint of grammar in NLP task, the sequence of user historical behaviors may contain multiple concurrent interests.
281: Rapid jumping and sudden ending over these interests causes the sequence data of user behaviors to seem to be noisy.
282: A possible direction is to design special structures to model such data in a sequence way.
283: We leave it for future research.
284: 5. Training Techniques
285: In the advertising system in Alibaba, numbers of goods and users scale up to hundreds of millions.
286: Practically, training industrial deep networks with large scale sparse input features is of great challenge.
287: In this section, we introduce two important techniques which are proven to be helpful in practice.
288: 5.1. Mini-batch Aware Regularization
289: Overfitting is a critical challenge for training industrial networks."
